title: Steam in Belgium
text: The progress which the Belgians have made in the establishment of steam power is very considerable. In this department of the arts, they have beat France -a statistical fact, of the most valuable nature. According to the statements, it appears that there are at this moment in the province of Liege, 216 steamengines in action, forming in the aggregate a power equal to that of 5445 horses. Of these 216, 137 are upon the right bank of the Meuse, and the aggregate power of these equals that of 2176 horses; the remaining 79 are upon the left bank, and their power equals that of 3269 horses. Of all these engines, three only are of foreign construction.

The largest of these steam-engines has a 300 horsepower; the weakest has one of about 12. None of the steam-engines of France has above a 100 horsepower. In the province of Liege, there are 18 engines with a power of from 100 to 300; 20 from 50 to 100;

38 from 20 to 50; 139 from 5 to 20; and one of 114. If we add the steam-power in action in the other Belgic provinces to that existing in Liege we find an aggregate force equal to that of about 20,000 horses. The most powerful engines, and the greatest number of them also, are to be found in Hainault, at Charleroi, and in the Borinage.

According to the statement published by authority in France, the 916 steam-engines in that country represent in the aggregate a power equal only to that of 14,051 horses. Those of Belgium exceed this, as we have seen, by nearly one-third. By comparing the respective numbers of inhabitants in the two countries, it will be found, that the manufacturing industry of Belgium, as shown by the preceding statements, is ten times more developed than that of France.
